name: Linux link spike in Docker
description:
Link examples/bodies for x64glibc inside a Docker container and see the process start. This gates every other milestone 1 task. No shader work here. The Metal shader string fails at runtime on GL, and that is expected.

Steps:
1. Write scripts/linux/Dockerfile: Ubuntu 24.04, X11 and GL dev headers, Mesa, xvfb, Odin dev-2026-08 linux-amd64 release, Roc nightly linux x86_64 2026-09-12-220fd47.
2. Mount the repo as a volume so outputs land in the gitignored platform/targets/ directories.
3. Build the sokol GLCORE debug archives for log, gfx, app and glue with sokol/build_clibs_linux.sh inside the container.
4. Build libhost.a with odin build -build-mode:static inside the container.
5. Copy the real CRT objects and shared libraries into platform/targets/x64glibc/: Scrt1.o, crti.o, crtn.o, libc.so.6, libm.so.6, libX11.so, libXi.so, libXcursor.so, libGL.so, plus whatever compiler-rt or libgcc file the Odin output needs. Roc's validator rejects undeclared files in that directory, so the list in main.roc must match.
6. Add an x64glibc entry to the targets: block in platform/main.roc with those inputs and app.
7. Run roc build in the container and start the binary once.

Fix the target names in docs/ROADMAP.md in this task: x64glibc and x64win, not x64linux.

Done when roc build succeeds for x64glibc in the container and the binary starts. Record in the result: the exact input list, the CRT and compiler-rt files needed, and any link errors and their fixes.

Part of 'Milestone 1: one source tree, three desktop targets'.
result:
Linked examples/bodies for x64glibc inside Docker and started the binary. ./scripts/linux/check.sh passes end to end (exit 0). Roc reported 0 errors on the link. Under xvfb the process opens the X11 window and GL context, then sokol_gfx aborts at shader validation (exit 134) because the Metal shader desc has no GLSL uniform members. That is the sokol-shdc task's job and the script treats 134 as the expected outcome for now.

Toolchain in the image: Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 under emulation on Apple silicon, odin dev-2026-08-nightly:902106f from the dev-2026-08 linux-amd64 release, roc nightly-2026-09-12-220fd47 linux x86_64.

Exact x64glibc input list, in order: Scrt1.o, crti.o, libhost.a, sokol_app_linux_x64_gl_debug.a, sokol_gfx_linux_x64_gl_debug.a, sokol_glue_linux_x64_gl_debug.a, sokol_log_linux_x64_gl_debug.a, app, libX11.so.6, libXi.so.6, libXcursor.so.1, libGL.so.1, libc.so.6, libm.so.6, crtn.o. All copied from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu in the image.

- No compiler-rt or libgcc file was needed. Zero unresolved symbols on the first link attempt.
- The shared libraries must be the soname-versioned files (libX11.so.6 and so on). The unversioned .so names are dev symlinks. lld records the soname as DT_NEEDED, confirmed with readelf.
- libdl and libpthread are inside libc.so.6 on glibc 2.39, so no separate files.
- The engine cross-checks for Linux from macOS with 'odin check engine -target:linux_amd64 -debug -vet -strict-style'. No Linux-specific compile errors.
- The macOS roc build still links with the x64glibc entry present and the x64glibc directory absent locally.
- Deviation from the plan: the script compiles the four sokol archives with the same flags as build_lib_x64_debug in sokol/build_clibs_linux.sh instead of running that script, which builds nine modules in four variants and needs ALSA headers.

name: Put the game calls behind a struct of procedures and test the protocol with a fake game
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Give the Seam a seam of its own. The four game calls become a struct of procedures. The Roc app satisfies it in the engine, and a fake game satisfies it in tests. Then test the call protocol in docs/DESIGN.md section 5 through seam_init, seam_step, seam_scenes and seam_shutdown.

## Steps

1. In engine/seam.odin, define Game_Calls: init(Config) -> rawptr, step(rawptr, Input, f32) -> rawptr, view(rawptr) -> Scene, drop_model(rawptr). Odin calling convention.
2. Add the Roc adapter: four one-line procedures that call roc_init, roc_step, roc_view and roc_drop_model from engine/roc_platform_abi.odin:373-378, and one value of Game_Calls that holds them. Put them in seam.odin or roc_runtime.odin; pick the file whose name says "this is the Roc side".
3. Change seam_init to take the Game_Calls and a Config. Store the calls on the Seam. In app.odin, call config_make(seed_from_env(), &g_state.renderer.meshes) and pass the result with the Roc adapter. The Seam stops importing the Mesh table.
4. Route every call in seam_step, seam_view and seam_shutdown through the stored Game_Calls. Keep the comments at seam.odin:125 and :157; they name the protocol.
5. Write engine/seam_test.odin with a fake game. The fake mirrors Roc's memory behaviour, from docs/DESIGN.md section 5:
   - A box is a roc_alloc of 8 header bytes plus the payload, alignment 8. The refcount is the int 8 bytes before the data pointer, set to 1. roc_incref_box in roc_platform_abi.odin:164 is public; the fake writes its own decrement and free, because the glue's release helpers are file-private and the glue is never edited by hand.
   - init allocates a box and returns it. It records the Config seed it saw and calls roc_decref on the Config, as Roc consumes it.
   - step reads the incoming box refcount, records the pointer, frees the box, allocates a new box, calls roc_decref on the Input, and returns the new box. Record the held and pressed contents before the decref.
   - view reads the refcount, records that it was 2, decrements it to 1, and returns a Scene whose draws list comes from roc_list_from_slice of one Draw. That is a real roc_alloc, like Roc.
   - drop_model records the pointer, reads the refcount, and frees the box.
   Keep the records in one package-level struct that each test resets.
6. Every test calls roc_heap_init(context.allocator) and defers roc_heap_shutdown(). Build the Config for seam_init with config_make on a table from mesh_table_init, or with an empty meshes list.
7. Write these tests through the Seam interface:
   - After seam_init, seam_scenes returns one Scene twice, init ran once with the seed given, and view ran once.
   - After one seam_step, prev is the Scene from init and curr is new. The box passed to step is the one init returned. The box passed to view is the one step returned. The refcount view saw was 2, and after seam_step it is 1.
   - After five steps with empty Input, the counters from roc_heap_counters advance by 2 allocs and 2 frees per step, no reallocs, and the live count is constant from the second step on. This is the rule scripts/alloc-check.sh checks.
   - A step with held and pressed slices delivers the same contents to the game, and adds one alloc and one free per non-empty list.
   - seam_shutdown calls drop_model once with the current box, and roc_heap_counters reports zero live blocks before roc_heap_shutdown.
   - The durations seam_step returns are non-negative.

## Constraints

- The fake lives in the test file only. The engine build must not reference it.
- Do not edit engine/roc_platform_abi.odin. It is generated by roc glue.
- Test names follow the existing style: test_<what>_<does what>.
- odin test engine -debug must still link. The Roc adapter references the foreign symbols the way seam.odin did before.

## Done when

- odin test engine -debug passes. The new tests are at least the six listed.
- git grep -n "roc_init\|roc_step\|roc_view\|roc_drop_model" engine returns only roc_platform_abi.odin and the Roc adapter.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh and scripts/host-check.sh pass on an idle machine.
- ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=120 roc run examples/entity-game/main.roc exits 0 with Frame Count: 120.
result:
Game_Calls (init, step, view, drop_model; Odin convention) lives in seam.odin. The Seam stores it; seam_init(s, calls, config) takes a ready Config and app.odin passes config_make(seed_from_env(), &meshes) with ROC_GAME. The Roc adapter ROC_GAME and its four file-private one-line procedures are in roc_runtime.odin (the Roc side). engine/seam_test.odin holds the fake game (boxes with an 8 byte refcount header, own decrement and free), records in one package struct g_fake, and seven tests through seam_init/seam_step/seam_scenes/seam_shutdown: first Scene pairs with itself, step rotates Scenes and hands view the new box at refcount 2 (1 after), a consumed box is never passed again over 5 steps, empty-Input steps make 2 allocs and 2 frees (1 free on the first step, which has no prev Scene) with constant live count, held/pressed contents reach the game with one extra alloc/free per list, shutdown drops the model once with zero live blocks, durations non-negative.

Deviation: the Odin test runner uses 10 threads and the Roc heap and fake records are globals, so seam_test.odin adds roc_heap_test_begin/roc_heap_test_end, which hold one mutex around roc_heap_init/roc_heap_shutdown. config_test.odin uses them too. Reworded one comment in config.odin that named roc_init so the grep criterion holds.

Checks:
- odin test engine -debug: 59 tests (52 + 7 new), all pass. Same with -vet -strict-style. The test binary still links.
- Mutations of seam.odin, each restored after: no incref before view (3 tests fail), no prev Scene decref (3 fail), held built from pressed (1 fails), no curr decref at shutdown (1 fails).
- git grep 'roc_init|roc_step|roc_view|roc_drop_model' engine: only roc_platform_abi.odin and roc_runtime.odin.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh: PASS cards dev/speed, entity-game dev/speed.
- scripts/host-check.sh: PASS.
- ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=120 roc run examples/entity-game/main.roc: Frame Count: 120, exit 0.

name: Research: give games named sokol key codes
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: research

Question: how should a game name a key instead of writing a sokol U16 literal?

Options to compare:
- A Keys package with one U16 constant per key (key_w : U16).
- A tag union (Key : [W, A, S, D, Space, ...]) with a to_code function.
- Either one generated from the Keycode enum in sokol-odin/sokol/app/app.odin by a script, so the codes cannot drift from sokol.

Constraints: Input carries List(U16). CONTEXT.md says key codes are sokol's and the game decides what a key means. Changing Input is a vocabulary change.

Answer with: the recommended option, its cost, and whether it needs a vocabulary change. Record the answer in the parent's Notes.
result: Recommend a nominal Key tag union (Key : [W, A, Space, Up, ...]) in packages/keys, with code : Key -> U16 and held/pressed helpers. A new build.roc step 'keys' generates Key.roc from the sokol Keycode enum (sokol-odin/sokol/app/app.odin:1584-1706), and the repo commits the output like the glue and shaders. Input stays List(U16), so it is not a vocabulary change. Sync: codes change only on a sokol-odin submodule bump; regenerate and check git diff --exit-code packages/keys, optionally in host-check.sh. A constants package (key_w : U16) only renames the literals; a U16 still takes any number. Gotchas: names need mapping (_0 to Num0, KP_0 to Kp0, LEFT_SHIFT to LeftShift, WORLD_1 to World1). A 120-tag match compiles fast (roc build 0.1 to 0.2 s). Key must be nominal so tags like Up and End do not clash. Escape still reaches games. Scratch prototypes: scratchpad/keys-research/.

name: rocco roadmap
description:
# rocco roadmap

Engineering milestones. Each milestone names what exists when it is done and
how to check it. Order matters: each one unlocks the next. `docs/DESIGN.md`
governs every entry here. If a milestone needs the design to change, change
the design first.

## Where the engine stands

Built and running:

- Fixed-timestep loop with an accumulator and interpolation.
- Three arenas by lifetime: permanent, level, frame. The level arena has no
  caller yet.
- Metal rendering through sokol: one pipeline, one cube mesh, index buffers,
  back-face culling, reversed-Z depth, one directional light.
- Camera with mouse look and quaternion orientation.
- The engine links as `libhost.a` into a Roc platform. Roc owns the script
  state. The host honours `roc_dealloc`. Hot reload works under `roc run`.
- The generated Odin ABI comes from `roc glue` with the spec in the
  `glue/` submodule (roc-odin-glue).

Not built: the generic platform in `docs/DESIGN.md`. The current
`platform/main.roc` names a concrete `Body` record. It is the last
game-specific header.

macOS only, today. Three things pin it there: the vertex and fragment shader
is a Metal Shading Language string in `render.odin`; the link inputs are the
Metal debug archives; and the sysroot script reads the Xcode SDK. Everything
else already goes through sokol, which has GL, D3D11 and Metal backends.

## Milestone 1: one source tree, three desktop targets

Cross-platform comes first, while the engine is small. Every line written
after this milestone lands in a file that already has a home per platform.
Doing it later means porting the host code that milestones 2 to 4 add.

Done when `examples/bodies` builds and runs on three hosts from one checkout,
with one host library per target:

- macOS arm64, natively, target `arm64mac`.
- Linux x64, inside the committed Docker image, target `x64glibc`, under
  `xvfb-run` with software GL and `ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES` set. Pass is exit
  code 0 and one printed frame count line.
- Windows x64, by hand on a Windows machine with Visual Studio Build Tools and
  a Windows SDK, target `x64win`.

The pattern is karl2d's, adapted to an engine that keeps sokol as the floor:

- One file per platform, selected by `#+build darwin`, `#+build linux`,
  `#+build windows`. No `when ODIN_OS` inside shared files. Each file holds
  the one real per-OS constant that exists today: the expected sokol backend,
  checked at init.
- Where a subsystem has more than one implementation, a struct of procedures
  per implementation and one constant chosen at compile time, with a
  `#config` override. karl2d does this for its render and audio backends and
  panics at compile time on an invalid name. rocco adds it when the audio
  backend or the file system arrives. Nothing has two implementations yet, so
  this milestone does not build the chooser.
- Shaders are compiled from one source to every backend at build time.
  sokol ships `sokol-shdc`, which emits an Odin file with MSL, GLSL and HLSL
  from one `.glsl` source. The generated file is committed. shdc is a
  dev-only tool.

What the Roc linker needs, found before the work started:

- A `targets:` input is only ever a file in `targets/<target>/`. There is no
  library-name syntax. Roc links with `-nostdlib`, so the platform lists
  every CRT object and library as a file, and the validator rejects
  undeclared files in that directory. Each OS gets a script that populates
  its directory. The macOS sysroot script is one of them.
- `x64glibc` refuses to link from a non-Linux host. `x64musl` cross-links
  from macOS but forces `-static`, and sokol needs shared X11 and GL. So the
  Linux binary is linked on a Linux host, in Docker.
- `x64win` needs a Windows SDK on the host. sokol's own Windows script needs
  `cl`. So the Windows binary is linked on Windows.
- No cross-compiling from one machine, then. Each host builds its own target.

1. Linux link spike in Docker. Write `scripts/linux/Dockerfile` with the
   pinned Odin and Roc Linux releases, the X11 and GL headers, Mesa and xvfb.
   Build the sokol `SOKOL_GLCORE` archives and the host library inside it.
   Copy the CRT objects and the shared libraries sokol needs into
   `platform/targets/x64glibc/`. Add the `x64glibc` entry to
   `platform/main.roc`. Link `examples/bodies` and see the process start. The
   shader fails on GL at this point, and that is expected. This step gates
   every other step. If it has no answer, stop and redesign.
2. Replace the MSL string with `sokol-shdc` output. Source in
   `engine/shaders/basic.glsl`, generated `engine/shader_basic.odin` with the
   command that made it in a comment at the top.
3. Add `engine/platform_darwin.odin`, `platform_linux.odin` and
   `platform_windows.odin`.
4. Write `scripts/build.roc` on basic-cli with the commands `inputs`, `glue`,
   `host`, `game <example>`, `shaders` and `all`. The target defaults to the
   host. A game author runs only `inputs` and `game`. Add the Windows input
   command that copies the SDK import libraries into
   `platform/targets/x64win/`. If Roc scripting blocks the milestone, fall
   back to a shell script.
5. Read `ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES` once at startup in the host. Set means quit
   cleanly after that many frames and print the count. Unset means run
   forever.
6. Run `examples/bodies` on Linux in Docker under `xvfb-run` with the exit
   switch. One wrapper command on the Mac builds the image and runs the check.
7. Build and run `examples/bodies` on Windows by hand. Add the `x64win` entry
   to `platform/main.roc`. Record the input list and the components installed.
8. Rewrite this section and the README with the results.

Steps 2 to 5 run in parallel after step 1. Step 6 needs all of them.

Check: three binaries from one tree. `git grep "when ODIN_OS"` returns only
the platform files. `git grep "SOKOL_METAL\|MTL"` returns nothing outside
`platform_darwin.odin` and the generated shader file.

Not in this milestone: web. The pinned Roc nightly has a `wasm32` target, but
Odin's JavaScript target and sokol's Emscripten path are separate work. Web
stays out of scope until the three desktop targets build from one tree.

Not in this milestone: CI and a published platform bundle. Both are alpha
work. See "Beside the milestones".

## Milestone 2: the platform stops naming the game

Done when `platform/main.roc` is the header in `docs/DESIGN.md` section
4 and both games in `docs/examples/` link and run against it.

1. Extend the glue spec in the `glue/` submodule with `Str`, `Box` as
   `rawptr`, and `List(U16)`. Check the output against the Zig glue for the
   same platform.
2. Write the host side of `Input`: fill `held` and `pressed` from the
   `down` and `prev` arrays each fixed step. Fill the mouse delta.
3. Write the host side of `Config`: a seed and a manifest with the three
   primitives, ids 1 to 3. Id 0 is the fallback.
4. Write the host side of `Scene`: keep two, pair draws by id, interpolate at
   render time, write one model matrix per draw.
5. Implement the call protocol in `docs/DESIGN.md` section 5. Count
   allocations with the tracking allocator. Expect one box shell alloc and
   free per step and no list copy.
6. Move the two games from `docs/examples/` to `examples/entity-game/` and
   `examples/cards/`, pointing at `../../platform/main.roc`. Build each with
   `roc build`. `libhost.a` must not rebuild between them.

Expect a `drop_model_for_host` export that frees the `Box(Model)` at shutdown
until `roc glue` emits box refcount helpers (roc issue 9536). roc-ray does the
same, and its `update_for_host!` unboxes the only reference so `update!` sees
uniquely referenced lists. That matches `docs/DESIGN.md` section 5.

Check: the allocator counters show in-place mutation. A change to either
game's `Model` does not touch `engine/`.

## Milestone 3: mesh handles and the manifest

Done when `Scene` draws by id resolve to more than one mesh.

1. Give the renderer a mesh table indexed by id. Load the three primitives
   into it at startup. Reserve id 0 for a magenta fallback cube.
2. Publish the table to `init` as the manifest.
3. Draw every entry in a `Scene` with its own mesh and transform.

Check: the entity game shows a cube player, sphere pickups and a slab door.
A misspelt mesh name draws magenta and logs once.

## Milestone 4: geometry from disk

Done when a Blender export appears in the manifest without an engine change.

1. Pick one format. glTF binary is the default choice. Load positions,
   normals and indices only.
2. Load every file in `assets/meshes/` into the level arena at startup. This
   is the first caller of the level arena.
3. Add each file to the manifest under its file stem.

Check: drop a new `.glb` into the directory, restart, name it from Roc, see
it. No rebuild of `libhost.a`.

## Milestone 5: entities in Roc

Done when the engine has no fixed scene array.

1. Delete the fixed `scene` array from the engine. The `Scene` from `view`
   is the only source of draws.
2. Entities live in the game's `Model` as a `List(Entity)` with explicit ids.
3. Parenting is a `parent : U64` field and a fold over the list. No pointer
   tree.

Check: the entity game creates and destroys entities at runtime. The renderer
never allocates per frame.

## Milestone 6: collision as data

Done when contacts cross the seam as a list.

1. The host computes swept AABB contacts from the current `Scene` bounds or
   from a `List(Collider)` the game returns in `Scene`. Decide which by
   measuring which is smaller at 1,000 entities.
2. `step` gains a third argument: `List(Contact)`. Update `Input` or add the
   list to it. This is a vocabulary change and rebuilds `libhost.a`.
3. The game decides what a contact means. The engine never does.

Check: the player stops at the door while it is closed.

## Milestone 7: one gameplay verb

Done when the entity game is playable start to finish.

1. Add one verb as a stage in the `step` pipeline with a test.
2. Add a win state to the `Model` and a `Scene` that shows it.

Check: a stranger plays it without instructions.

## Beside the milestones

Slot these in when they pay for themselves. Do not run them as a block.

- **Debug drawing.** Lines, wireframe, text. `Scene` gains a `lines` list.
  This is a vocabulary change.
- **Audio.** `saudio` calls back on another thread against a deadline. The
  game returns what should be heard as data. The first command with a
  duration probably arrives here.
- **Shader loading and reload.** After milestone 1 the shader is a
  `sokol-shdc` output. Reload means re-running the compiler and swapping the
  pipeline; the platform files decide how each OS watches the file.
- **The allocation pool.** A fixed region reserved once at startup with a
  free list behind `roc_alloc` and `roc_dealloc`. Removes the system heap
  from the step path. Satisfies static allocation. Measure before and after
  with the tracking allocator.
- **Debug and speed parity.** Run the allocator counters under both
  `--opt=dev` and `--opt=speed` after every memory change.

Alpha work, once the experiment earns it and not before milestone 2 is done:

- **CI.** GitHub Actions with one runner per OS. Roc refuses `x64glibc` from
  a non-Linux host and `x64win` needs a Windows SDK, so no single runner
  builds all three. Each job runs the build script for its host, runs
  `examples/bodies` under a virtual display with `ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES`,
  and runs `roc check` and `roc test` on every app under `examples/` and
  `docs/examples/`. The Linux job reuses `scripts/linux/Dockerfile`.
- **A published platform bundle.** `roc bundle` into a release asset holding
  every target directory with prebuilt host libraries, as roc-ray does. A
  game header points at the URL and the author runs `roc main.roc` with
  nothing but Roc installed. Needs committable Linux inputs: checked-in CRT
  objects and assembly stubs for libc, libm and the X11 libraries instead of
  copies from a container. Windows import libraries can come from MinGW
  `.def` files through `zig dlltool`, so no SDK at bundle time.

## Out of scope

- A Vulkan or Metal backend by hand. sokol is the floor.
- Networking.
- An editor.
- Dynamics beyond simple collision until milestone 4 is done.
- Web builds until the three desktop targets build from one tree and Odin
  and sokol have a shared web path.
- CI and a published platform bundle until alpha.
- A scripting API where Roc calls the engine. Roc returns descriptions. The
  engine acts on them.

name: Move the draw loop and the Pairing into engine/frame_render.odin
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Create the Frame render module with the same picture as today. This subtask moves code. It adds no seam and no test.

## Steps

1. Add "Frame render" to CONTEXT.md under Time, after Frame. Say: the host module that turns the previous Scene, the current Scene and the Alpha into one submitted draw per Draw. It owns the Pairing. Avoid: renderer, draw loop, presenter, scene renderer.
2. Rename engine/scene.odin to engine/frame_render.odin. Rename engine/scene_test.odin to engine/frame_render_test.odin. Keep every helper and test.
3. Add a Frame_Render struct to frame_render.odin. Give it the Pairing. Add frame_render_init(fr, perm allocator) and frame_render_destroy(fr). Move the pairing_init and pairing_destroy calls there from seam_init and seam_shutdown.
4. Move draw_scene from app.odin:130 into frame_render.odin as the one draw call of the module. Give it the Frame_Render, the previous Scene, the current Scene, the Alpha, the view-projection matrix and the Mesh table. Build the Pairing from the previous Scene at the top of that call, once per Frame. Delete the pairing_build call and the pairing field from seam_step and the Seam struct.
5. Move scene_view_proj, LIGHT_DIR, SCENE_NEAR and UP from app.odin into frame_render.odin. Add one camera read to the Frame render that takes the previous Scene, the current Scene, the Alpha and the aspect ratio and returns the view-projection matrix. It composes camera_lerp and scene_view_proj.
6. Add seam_scenes(s) that returns (prev, curr). Keep the rule at seam.odin:155: before the first step the one Scene pairs with itself. Delete seam_prev if nothing else calls it. Change app.odin:96-97 to call seam_scenes.
7. Make frame_cb in app.odin a composition root: run the fixed steps, begin the pass, pick the view-projection matrix from the debug camera or the Frame render camera read, call the Frame render draw call, end the pass. Add Frame_Render to State.
8. Update docs/ROADMAP.md:182 from "once per fixed step" to "once per frame, from the previous Scene".

## Constraints

- The Pairing keeps its capacity across Frames. pairing_build clears the map and never frees it. Do not allocate per Frame.
- The fallback ignores the tint. Keep the comment at app.odin:129 with the code it describes.
- Do not change the Seam call protocol in docs/DESIGN.md section 5.
- No new comments that restate the code. Keep the ones that name a constraint.

## Done when

- odin test engine passes with the same test count as before.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh passes for cards and entity-game: 2 allocs and 2 frees per step, constant live count.
- scripts/host-check.sh passes.
- ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=120 roc run examples/entity-game/main.roc exits 0 and prints Frame Count: 120.
- A run by eye with ROCCO_DEBUG_CAMERA=1 still flies, and the sprout still turns smoothly without it.
- git grep draw_scene returns nothing under engine/app.odin.
result: Moved draw_scene into engine/frame_render.odin as frame_render_draw, with frame_render_camera as the camera read. Frame_Render owns the Pairing and builds it once per frame from the previous Scene. The Seam lost its pairing field; seam_scenes replaces seam_prev. seam_init lost its now-unused perm allocator parameter. CONTEXT.md gains Frame render; ROADMAP Pairing note says once per frame. Verified: odin test engine -debug 45/45 (same as before); roc test on cards and entity-game pass; alloc-check PASS for both games at dev and speed; host-check PASS; entity game ran 120 frames, exit 0, Frame Count: 120; git grep draw_scene engine/app.odin is empty. By-eye check with and without ROCCO_DEBUG_CAMERA=1 left to the maintainer.

name: Slim the Seam to the call protocol
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Deepen the Seam so it owns exactly the call protocol in docs/DESIGN.md section 5: one Model pointer and two Scenes, behind init, step, scenes and shutdown. Today engine/seam.odin also owns the tracking allocator, the six Roc runtime hooks, the alloc report line and its step counter. roc_alloc reads g_state.seam.heap, so engine/config_test.odin:35 pokes a Seam field to build a Config. seam_step calls the foreign symbols roc_init, roc_step, roc_view and roc_drop_model directly, which only the linked Roc app defines, so the protocol has no test.

Vocabulary: module, interface, seam, adapter, locality (codebase-design skill). Domain words: CONTEXT.md. This is candidate 2 of the architecture review of 2026-09-30, agreed by the maintainer.

## Done when

- engine/roc_runtime.odin owns the Roc heap: the tracking allocator, the alloc, dealloc and realloc counters, and the six exported hooks. Nothing else in the engine reads the allocator or the counters except through its interface.
- engine/seam.odin holds a Seam struct of the game calls, the Model pointer, the two Scenes and has_prev, and nothing else. Its interface is seam_init, seam_step, seam_scenes, seam_shutdown.
- The four game calls sit behind a struct of procedures. Two adapters satisfy it: the Roc app in the engine, a fake game in engine/seam_test.odin.
- seam_test.odin tests the protocol through the Seam interface with the fake game: Scenes rotate, the consumed box is never reused, the box refcount is 1 after every step, each step makes 2 allocs and 2 frees with empty Input, shutdown drops the Model once and leaves no live block.
- config_test.odin initialises the Roc heap through its interface instead of poking a field.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh parses the same report line, byte for byte, and passes. host-check passes and reports the host library unchanged. The entity game runs 120 frames and exits 0.

## Decisions so far

- Name: Roc heap. docs/DESIGN.md section 1 already says Odin owns "the Roc heap, the six hooks". Add the term to CONTEXT.md under Memory lifetimes: the host allocator behind roc_alloc, roc_dealloc and roc_realloc, with the tracking allocator that records each size because roc_realloc carries no old size. Avoid: Roc allocator, host heap, seam heap.
- The Roc heap is one package global in roc_runtime.odin, not a field of the app State. The hooks are exported "c" procedures with no user data, so a global is unavoidable. Tests initialise it through roc_heap_init and tear it down through roc_heap_shutdown.
- The game calls struct uses Odin calling convention. The Roc adapter is four one-line procedures that call the foreign "c" symbols. A fake game then gets a context and can allocate.
- seam_init takes the game calls and a ready Config. app.odin calls config_make and passes the result. The Seam stops knowing the seed and the Mesh table.
- seam_step returns the step and view durations. app.odin keeps the step counter and the report flag, and prints the report line through a procedure in roc_runtime.odin that reads the counters. The line format is a contract with scripts/alloc-check.sh and does not change.
- The leak report at shutdown moves with the tracking allocator into roc_heap_shutdown.
- The hooks keep setting context = g_state.ctx. Changing that is not in scope.
- Not in scope: the allocation pool (task 4vqu0dcl), Commands, Contacts, reading run options once. After this task each of those edits one file.

## Order

Subtasks run in priority order. Each one leaves the engine building and the checks passing.

name: Put one submit call at the seam of the Frame render and test the composition
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Give the Frame render one submit call at its seam. Satisfy it with two adapters: sokol in the engine, a recording adapter in tests. Then test the composition through the Frame render interface. Today only the helpers have tests. Nobody tests that a Draw with no partner draws at itself, that the first Frame pairs with itself, or that the fallback mesh ignores the tint.

## Steps

1. Define the submit procedure type in frame_render.odin. It takes a context pointer, the resolved Mesh pointer, the vertex uniforms and the fragment uniforms. Vs_Params and Fs_Params come from shader_basic.odin. Store a procedure pointer and its context on Frame_Render.
2. Make renderer_draw in render.odin the sokol adapter. app.odin sets it on the Frame render at init, after renderer_init. render.odin keeps the pipeline setup and the submit only.
3. Move the Vertex struct from render.odin to mesh.odin. gltf.odin and mesh.odin use it. render.odin does not.
4. Write a recording adapter in frame_render_test.odin. It appends one record per submit: the Mesh pointer, the model matrix, the tint. A test builds a Mesh_Table with mesh_table_init only. It never uploads, so no sokol setup is needed. mesh_resolve returns a pointer into the table, so a test compares the recorded pointer with the table slot.
5. Build Scenes in tests from Odin slices. Roc_List fields are elements and length. A test may point elements at a stack array, because the Frame render only reads. Do not call roc_alloc: it reads g_state.
6. Write these tests through the Frame render draw call:
   - A Draw whose id has a partner in the previous Scene interpolates position and yaw at the Alpha.
   - A Draw whose id has no partner draws at its own position.
   - When the previous Scene is the current Scene, every Draw draws at itself.
   - A Draw with mesh id 0, or an id past the table, submits the fallback slot with a white tint.
   - A Draw with a known mesh id submits that slot with its own tint.
   - Two Draws that share an id in the previous Scene pair with the first one.
   - The camera read returns a matrix built from the interpolated eye and target and the new fov_y. Compare against scene_view_proj of the expected Camera_Pose.
7. Keep the helper tests for yaw_lerp, draw_transform, camera_lerp and the Pairing. They test internal seams and are cheap.

## Constraints

- One procedure pointer, not a struct of procedures. Milestone 1 chose a struct of procedures for backends that a build picks at compile time. This seam is swapped at runtime by a test, and one procedure is enough.
- The engine build must not reference the recording adapter. It lives in the test file only.
- Test names follow the existing style: test_<what>_<does what>.

## Done when

- odin test engine passes. The new tests are at least the seven listed.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh and scripts/host-check.sh pass.
- ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=120 roc run examples/entity-game/main.roc exits 0.
- A run by eye shows the same picture as before this task.
- git grep Vertex engine/render.odin returns nothing.
result: Submit is one procedure type (ctx, mesh, Vs_Params, Fs_Params) stored with submit_ctx on Frame_Render. renderer_draw is the sokol adapter, set in init_cb after renderer_init. name: Frame render: one owner for the Scene-to-pixels path
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

Deepen the host side of the render into one module, the Frame render. Today the path from a Scene to pixels spans five files. draw_scene in engine/app.odin:130 knows the Roc_List layout, the Pairing, the interpolation, the Mesh table, the fallback tint rule and the shader uniforms. render.odin is a ten-line pass-through to sokol. The Seam owns the Pairing and builds it every fixed step, though only the last one of a Frame is drawn. Nobody tests the composition.

Vocabulary: module, interface, seam, adapter, locality (codebase-design skill). Domain words: CONTEXT.md.

## Done when

- One module, the Frame render, in engine/frame_render.odin, takes the previous Scene, the current Scene, the Alpha and a view-projection matrix, and submits every Draw.
- The Frame render owns the Pairing and builds it once per Frame from the previous Scene. The Seam holds only the Model and the two Scenes.
- One submit call sits at the seam of the Frame render. Two adapters satisfy it: sokol in the engine, a recording adapter in tests.
- engine/frame_render_test.odin tests the composition through that interface: partner interpolation, no partner, first Frame, fallback ignores tint.
- app.odin is a composition root. draw_scene, scene_view_proj, LIGHT_DIR, SCENE_NEAR and UP leave it.
- The picture does not change. odin test, roc test, scripts/alloc-check.sh and scripts/host-check.sh pass on arm64mac. The entity game runs 120 frames and exits 0.

## Decisions so far

- Name: Frame render. Add the term to CONTEXT.md under Time, beside Frame.
- The Frame render takes a view-projection matrix, not a camera. The debug camera builds its own matrix and bypasses the Scene camera, so the camera choice stays in app.odin. The camera lerp and scene_view_proj move into the Frame render as its camera read.
- Pairing runs once per Frame, not once per fixed step. docs/ROADMAP.md:182 says "once per fixed step". That line records a mechanism, not a semantic. Update it. DESIGN.md sections 2 and 5 do not change.
- The submit adapter is a procedure pointer on the Frame render struct, so a test can swap it at runtime. Milestone 1 chose a struct of procedures per implementation for backends; one procedure is enough here.
- scene.odin merges into frame_render.odin. Its helpers (Pairing, draw_transform, camera_lerp, yaw_lerp) become internal seams of the Frame render. They stay package-visible so their existing tests keep running. New tests hit the Frame render interface.
- render.odin stays as the sokol adapter: the pipeline and the submit. Vertex moves to mesh.odin, because gltf.odin and mesh.odin use it and render.odin does not.
- The Seam gains one read that returns (prev, curr), so app.odin stops reading seam.curr as a field. Nothing else in the Seam changes. Slimming the rest of the Seam is a separate candidate.

## Order

Subtasks run in priority order. Each one leaves the engine building and the checks passing. Debug drawing (task czru7n07) lands in this module and is blocked on this task.

The Seam keeps only the Model and the two Scenes. Seven composition tests cover partner interpolation, no partner, one Scene, fallback tint, known mesh, shared id and the camera read. Rename the Roc package Meshes to Mesh, and its function named to resolve. Agreed with the maintainer on 2026-09-30.

Why: Roc modules are singular nouns for the thing they operate on (Str, List, Dict), and the sibling package is already Camera. Mesh.primitive(config, Cube) and Mesh.resolve(config, "sprout") read as "a mesh". The word named says nothing about what the function does. The function looks a name up in the manifest, and CONTEXT.md already calls that step "resolve": the game resolves the names it needs once, in init. The fallback to id 0 reads naturally on a resolve.

Not in scope: a hosted Mesh.load(path). docs/DESIGN.md section 6 refuses hosted functions. The engine loads every .glb in assets/meshes/ at startup, and the game only resolves names. A description of wanted assets can come when levels arrive; nothing needs it today.

## Steps

1. Rename the directory packages/meshes/ to packages/mesh/ with git mv. Rename Meshes.roc to Mesh.roc.
2. In packages/mesh/main.roc, change the header to package [Mesh] {} and the import to Mesh.
3. In packages/mesh/Mesh.roc, rename the module to Mesh, rename named to resolve, and update every expect. Keep the signature: resolve : Config, Str -> U32. The config argument stays, because the function is pure and reads the manifest. Keep the dbg on a miss and the fallback to 0.

6. Update the comments that name the package path: engine/config_test.odin:25, scripts/alloc-check.sh:22, scripts/build.roc:200.
7. Run git grep -n -e Meshes -e packages/meshes -e "\.named(" -- ':!glue' ':!sokol-odin' ':!.dex' ':!engine/roc_platform_abi.odin'. Fix every hit. The glue names Roc_Init_Arg0_Meshes after the Config field, not the package; leave the glue and engine/vocabulary.odin alone.

name: Fix GL clip-space depth with sokol-shdc fixup_clipspace
description:
Add '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' to the @vs block in engine/shaders/basic.glsl and regenerate engine/shader_basic.odin with the command in its header.

Why: the projection in engine/math.odin (mat4_perspective_reversed_infinite) produces Metal and D3D11 style clip depth, z_clip in [0, w]. GL expects [-w, w]. sokol's GL backend never calls glClipControl, so on Linux the depth buffer holds 0.5 + near/(2d) instead of near/d. Ordering stays correct, so the picture looks right, but the reversed-Z precision is gone and far objects z-fight. The shdc option rewrites gl_Position.z in the GLSL output only. Metal and HLSL output are untouched. This keeps the projection and the pipeline desc backend-neutral, which is the rule for milestone 1: clip-space differences are resolved in the shader source, never in Odin.

Rejected alternative: glClipControl(GL_LOWER_LEFT, GL_ZERO_TO_ONE) from platform_linux.odin. Needs a GL function loader in Odin and GL 4.5.

Steps:
1. Add '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' as the first line inside '@vs vs'.
2. Regenerate with sokol-shdc (command in the README and the generated header).
3. Confirm the GLSL 430 block in the generated file gains a gl_Position.z rewrite and the MSL and HLSL blocks are unchanged apart from that.
4. Build on macOS with -vet -strict-style and run examples/bodies: no sokol errors, same picture.
5. Run ./scripts/linux/check.sh: process runs under xvfb.

Done when the generated GLSL contains the clip-space rewrite, macOS still renders, and the Linux check passes. Record in the result the exact generated line.

Part of 'Milestone 1: one source tree, three desktop targets'. Found while reviewing how the pipeline desc behaves across backends: sokol maps face_winding, cull_mode and depth compare per backend, but not clip-space depth.
result: Added '@glsl_options fixup_clipspace' to @vs vs in engine/shaders/basic.glsl and regenerated engine/shader_basic.odin with sokol-shdc 11d0cf6. Generated GLSL 430 line: 'gl_Position.z = 2.0 * gl_Position.z - gl_Position.w;'. MSL and HLSL sources are byte-identical. macOS: host builds with -vet -strict-style, bodies runs with no sokol errors. Linux: ./scripts/linux/check.sh exit 0, process ran under xvfb to the timeout. Correction to the rationale: GL window depth now equals near/d, the same as Metal and D3D11, so depth values match across backends. The fixup does not restore float reversed-Z precision: GL still computes (ndc+1)/2 with ndc near -1 for far objects, and the default depth buffer is probably 24-bit unorm. That precision needs glClipControl(ZERO_TO_ONE) and a D32F target.

name: Command list: pure requests for host-side lifetime
description:
Add a List(Command) to the value that step returns. The game asks for a one-time
host action as data. Odin runs each command after step returns. The seam stays
pure: no hosted block, no `=>` function, no `!` name on the Roc side.

## Why

docs/DESIGN.md section 6 refuses hosted functions until a pure value cannot
express the need. docs/GLOSSARY.md (description vs command) says a Scene is a
description and a Spawn or PlaySound is a command. A description says what
should exist every frame. A command says do this once. Things with host-side
lifetime, such as a sound with a duration or a physics body with a warm-start
cache, need a command.

Compare roc-ray: its app calls `Draw.rectangle!` and other host effects
directly through a hosted block. rocco refuses that model. Every effect crosses
the seam outward as a value. This keeps replay from an `(Input, dt)` log
working and keeps `roc test` able to run step without an engine.

## Approach

1. Define `Command` as a tag union in the platform header. Start with the
   smallest set a real game needs. Likely first tags: `PlaySound(sound_id)`,
   `Spawn(id, ...)`, `Destroy(id)`. Do not add a tag until a game needs it.
2. Change the step return type from `Model` to `{ model : Model, commands :
   List(Command) }`. Keep init and view unchanged.
3. Write the host side. Odin decodes the list after step, runs each command
   in list order, then discards the list. Add the tag union layout to the
   roc-odin-glue spec.
4. Keep description first. If a need can be expressed as a Scene field, add
   the Scene field instead of a command.
5. Add one example game stage that emits a command and one `roc test` that
   asserts the command list for a given input.

## Ordering

Do this when the first thing with host-side lifetime arrives. The roadmap
expects that to be audio (task: Audio via saudio, returned as data). Do not
build this before Milestone 2 lands, because the step signature is still
changing there.

## Acceptance

- The platform header declares Command and step returns the commands list.
- No `hosted` block and no `=>` signature exists in platform/main.roc.
- The host runs commands in list order after step and frees the list.
- `roc test` on the example game asserts at least one emitted command.
- A replay of a recorded `(Input, dt)` log produces the same command lists.
- docs/DESIGN.md section 6 and the GLOSSARY description/command entry match
  the shipped shape.

name: Simplify the macOS sysroot script to keep the SDK layout
description:
Rewrite scripts/make-macos-sysroot.sh so that it copies SDK framework stubs with their real layout. Remove the re-export stripping and the objc.framework trick.

Why: the header of the script is wrong for Roc nightly-2026-09-12-220fd47. An LLD_REPRODUCE capture of 'roc build' shows that Roc passes -syslibroot platform/targets/macos-sysroot, -F <sysroot>/System/Library/Frameworks, -L <sysroot>/usr/lib and -lSystem. Re-exports failed only because the script writes a flat Foo.framework/Foo.tbd. lld resolves each re-export by its install name under the syslibroot, for example AppKit.framework/Versions/C/AppKit.tbd.

Evidence from the experiment:
- Sysroot = the Xcode SDK itself: the link fails. Roc emits one -framework per framework in the sysroot. QTKit and JavaNativeFoundation are Intel-only, SwiftUICore refuses clients, and Message does not resolve. So the script must still pick the frameworks.
- Sysroot = the 16-framework closure copied with 'cp -R -P' from the SDK (Versions/ and symlinks kept, nothing stripped), plus usr/lib/libSystem*.tbd and usr/lib/libobjc*.tbd, and no objc.framework: the link passes and bodies.bin runs. otool -L shows /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, linked through the Foundation re-export.

Steps:
1. Keep the closure walk over reexported-libraries. Re-exported frameworks must exist in the sysroot, or lld cannot resolve them.
2. For each framework in the closure, copy only the .tbd files and the symlinks that point to them: Foo.framework/Foo.tbd -> Versions/Current/Foo.tbd, Versions/Current -> <V>, and Versions/<V>/Foo.tbd. Do not copy Headers or Modules. A full 'cp -R -P' copy is 33 MB, mostly headers.
3. Copy usr/lib/libSystem.tbd, libSystem.B.tbd, libobjc.tbd and libobjc.A.tbd, with their symlinks.
4. Delete strip_reexports and the objc.framework block.
5. Rewrite the header comment. Keep one real constraint: Roc links every framework in the sysroot, so the sysroot holds only the frameworks the host needs.
6. Run 'roc scripts/build.roc -- all' from an empty platform/targets/macos-sysroot and run examples/bodies.

Done when examples/bodies links and runs with the new sysroot, 'otool -L examples/bodies/bodies.bin' lists /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, and the script has no stripping code.

Related: a Zulip question asks whether a platform header can name its frameworks. If Roc adds that, the sysroot can become the SDK path and this script can go.

A thin effect layer runs them. Target carries an extra_inputs tag (MacSdk, WindowsSdk, BuiltInDocker), so inputs matches on the tag, not on the target name.

Per target:
- macOS inputs: copies the 4 sokol Metal debug archives, copies libclang_rt.osx.a from 'xcrun clang -print-resource-dir'/lib/darwin, and runs scripts/make-macos-sysroot.sh. The sysroot step is extra: before, it was README step 0, and the game author needs it.
- Windows inputs (the Windows input script): copies the 4 sokol D3D11 debug .lib archives and kernel32, user32, gdi32, shell32, ole32, d3d11 and dxgi from the newest %ProgramFiles(x86)%/Windows Kits/10/Lib/<ver>/um/x64, the same rule as basic-cli find_windows_sdk_lib_dir. The Windows host is host.lib (basic-cli naming). NOT RUN: there is no Windows machine. No CRT libraries are copied yet. The Windows task description now says to settle the list there.
- Linux inputs: exits 1 with 'Linux inputs are built in Docker. Run ./scripts/linux/check.sh.' The Linux task adds this command.

Deviation: steps run with Cmd.exec_cmd! (inherited stdio), not Cmd.run! with Tee. Tee gives the child a pipe, not a terminal, and run! cancels the child once captured output passes 16 MiB. exec_cmd! streams live and returns an error on a nonzero exit. The script maps that error to '<program> exited with <code>' and stops.

Found during the run: host needs platform/targets/<target>/ to exist, and all runs host before inputs. The host step now creates the directory first.

The copied sokol archives, libclang_rt.osx.a and sysroot are byte-identical to the previous hand-made ones. bodies.bin runs (4 to 5 s, about 500 to 650 frame lines, no errors).

- Code review (standards + spec) applied: xcrun clang instead of PATH clang, parse returns the step list (no unreachable All arm), Step instead of Command (the glossary reserves Command), a per-target extra_inputs tag, plain failure messages, and a README fix for the game-author paragraph.
